summary: Ground cab on Purcell Mountain near Randle, WA, built 1933; abandoned in the 1950s and removed or destroyed in the 1960s; no source describes what remains.

facts.status_note: Cab abandoned in the 1950s and removed or destroyed in the 1960s; no source describes what remains on the site
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Gifford Pinchot National Forest

access.note: On National Forest land; the road is blocked near 4,480 ft and the summit trail is not maintained. No closure notice was found in these sources.

visit.trail_note: Road blocked near 4,480 ft at the west ridge; the guide's northwest route is 1.5 miles one way with about 1,000 ft of gain. No structure is described as standing.

events.note: Ground cab (standard ground cabin); four sources give 1933
Panoramic photographs taken on 22 July 1934 from 10 feet above the ground on top of the cab; photographer recorded only as J.D.R.
Coast and Geodetic Survey station stamped Purcell Mtn. 1946 described as 8 feet southeast of the southeast corner of the lookout house, so a lookout house stood on the summit in 1946
Abandoned in the 1950s per the register, firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb; 1950 is the decade start used as a placeholder, no exact year is given
Removed in the 1960s per the register and the Washington lookouts listing; firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed. 1960 is the decade start used as a placeholder, no exact year is given
Registered March 17, 2011 as FFLOS US 859, WA 54; nominated by Irene Potter

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the Washington lookouts listing say removed in the 1960s; firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed in the 1960s. All four agree on the decade and no source gives the method or a date, so the story reports both wordings.

The register, firelookout.com and IamWho's location data give 5,442 feet, while WillhiteWeb gives a summit elevation of 5,422 feet. No source explains the 20-foot difference, so the story gives both figures.

notes_for_editor: No primary Forest Service or newspaper record was read. The WebSearch budget for this run was used up before any search could run, so staffing, notable fires and the current site condition are unknown; the story says so. The access level 'public' is inferred from National Forest status and a climbing guide, not a closure notice; check the Gifford Pinchot National Forest before relying on it. The 1946 survey text comes from a copy on the Washington lookouts page; the NGS datasheet (PID SB1035) was not fetched. Location data disagree on section (weebly 13N-8E-30; IamWho T13N R8E S20) and on the photo elevation (IamWho lists 5450 feet beside 5442 feet), so neither is used. The 1934 IamWho panoramas are credited to the National Archives Pacific Northwest Region but state no licence, so none are added to photos. The brief's record needs no correction on what was checked; the firetower map image in its source_pages returns HTTP 404.
